verdicts.why: Blake works directly for Fisk and is killed by Fisk's fixer; in S2#8 BB reveals the Fisk organization's role in his murder, which helps bring Fisk down, so the stage text is accurate and the tie's consequence for Fisk is huge.
Skye names Micro on screen as one of her sources and relays the lead he passed her, which is a connection implied by dialogue; the wiki identifies this Rising Tide Micro as David Lieberman.
Family tie never met: Dorothy Walker dies years before Danielle is born and the two never share a scene or any dealing.
Blood tie never met: James Lucas does not appear with Danielle or come up with her anywhere on screen.
Family tie never met: Trish is never seen with Danielle or mentioned around her, and nothing on screen implies they know each other.
Father and daughter who meet on screen (reunited in S2#8); Danielle first appears in S2#6 with Luke referenced there, so the family stage stands as written.
Kilgrave takes over Costa's precinct and makes him hold his own gun to his head, leaving him with nightmares he recounts to Jessica; a direct, life-shaping dealing.

value.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3#16
value.text: James lived in Afterlife under Jiaying, where Gordon serves as her teleporter, until he is cast out. Years later he admits he always assumed Jiaying would send Gordon to come for him.
value.on_a_card_about_b: A former Afterlife resident who expects Gordon to come for him.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Afterlife's teleporter, the one he expects Jiaying to send.

verdicts.why: Both served Jiaying's Afterlife circle and James names Gordon in dialogue as the man he expected to come for him; the text is narrowed because Gordon personally bringing him in is not clearly shown.
Knowing about someone: Hartley only hears Fury's order secondhand through Bobbi, and nothing on screen implies she and Fury have ever dealt with each other.
Both serve Fisk's inner circle, and Wesley is at Melvin's workshop with Fisk while Melvin fits Owlsley's armor; the wiki lists Wesley among Melvin's enemies.

The tie stays for now: Mace deals with Ward only inside the Framework, where Ward is a digital copy of a dead man, and the rules don't say whether a simulated version counts as knowing the real person.
Karen deliberately sends McCaffrey the Red Hook charter, which the governor uses to threaten Fisk, and in S2#8 McCaffrey attends Karen's trial and is locked in the courthouse with her.
Jessica is in the room and fights Trish while Trish holds Kith hostage, a direct on-screen dealing.

value.title: Daredevil: Born Again S2#3
value.text: Connor Powell orders the Anti-Vigilante Task Force to open fire on the prisoners escaping Red Hook, Jack Duquesne among them.
value.on_a_card_about_b: An escaping prisoner Powell orders his officers to shoot.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Task force leader who orders his officers to fire on Jack's escape.

verdicts.why: Powell runs the Red Hook site holding Jack and orders his officers to fire on the escape; the text is corrected because Powell gives the order rather than being one of several shooters.
Turk works for Fisk's organization, is paid through Wesley for luring Vladimir into Fisk's trap and says he is happy to work for Fisk, and is arrested when Fisk's empire is exposed.
